kept.excerpt: Divulgada neste sábado, 19, a nova pesquisa Paraná Pesquisas para o governo do Rio Grande do Sul mostra o deputado federal Zucco (PL) na liderança, com 36,4% das intenções de voto. Ele é seguido por Juliana Brizola (PDT), que marca 31,3% no cenário estimulado. O atual vice-governador Gabriel Souza (MDB) aparece na terceira colocação, tendo avançado para 12,9%. A pesquisa Paraná Pesquisas entrevistou 1.352 eleitores entre 16 e 18 de setembro de 2026, por meio de entrevistas pessoais, domiciliares e presenciais.
kept.relevance: The most recent verified poll included before the cutoff puts Zucco numerically ahead, with a 2.7-percentage-point margin of error and TSE registration RS-00319/2026.

kept.excerpt: Real Time Big Data's September 10 poll put Zucco at 36%, Juliana Brizola at 35%, and Gabriel Souza at 22% in the stimulated first-round contest. In a simulated runoff, Zucco and Brizola each received 44%; Zucco received 45% against Souza's 40% in another matchup. The survey interviewed 1,600 Rio Grande do Sul voters between September 5 and 9, with a two-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence. It was registered with the TSE under RS-05497/2026.
kept.relevance: Direct runoff polling shows that Zucco's first-round position did not translate into a clear advantage over Brizola.

kept.excerpt: Quaest's August 24 survey put Luciano Zucco at 26% and Juliana Brizola at 23%, a technical tie within its three-percentage-point margin of error. In a simulated runoff between them, Brizola received 36% and Zucco 33%. Quaest interviewed 900 voters in person between August 20 and 23. The poll was registered with the TSE under RS-06875/2026.
kept.relevance: An independent pollster provides a different measurement of the close race and an earlier runoff benchmark.

kept.excerpt: Paraná Pesquisas reported Zucco at 34.4%, Juliana Brizola at 31.4%, and Gabriel Souza at 11.3% in its August first-round survey. The survey did not simulate runoff scenarios. It interviewed 1,504 voters in person between August 18 and 20, with a 2.6-percentage-point margin of error and 95% confidence. It was commissioned by the institute itself and registered with the TSE under RS-03898/2026.
kept.relevance: This same-pollster baseline helps assess whether the September figures represent substantial movement or broadly stable candidate support.

kept.excerpt: O PL (Partido Liberal) no Rio Grande do Sul oficializou nesta quarta-feira (22) a candidatura do deputado federal Luciano Zucco ao governo do estado. A chapa formada para rivalizar com Juliana Brizola (PDT) — apoiada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — foi costurada há meses com os cinco maiores partidos do campo da direita no estado: PL, PP-União Brasil, Republicanos, Novo e Podemos. Integram a chapa como vice a deputada estadual Silvana Covatti (PP) e, para o Senado, os deputados federais Ubiratan Sanderson (PL) e Marcel Van Hattem (Novo).
kept.relevance: Confirms Zucco's nomination, running mate, and supporting party coalition, establishing the organizational backing for his candidacy.

kept.excerpt: As Eleições de 2026 estão marcadas para o dia 4 de outubro, quando eleitoras e eleitores vão às urnas para eleger ocupantes dos cargos de presidente da República, governadores, senadores e deputados federais, estaduais e distritais, no caso do Distrito Federal. O segundo turno do pleito está marcado para o dia 25 de outubro. De 20 de julho a 5 de agosto, partidos e federações realizam convenções partidárias para deliberar sobre coligações e escolher candidatas e candidatos que concorrerão aos cargos de presidente e vice-presidente da República, governador e vice-governador, senador e respectivos suplentes, bem como aos cargos de deputado federal, estadual e distrital nas Eleições de 2026.
kept.publisher: Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Santa Catarina (TRE-SC)
kept.relevance: An official electoral-justice source confirms the first-round and runoff schedule applicable to the Rio Grande do Sul gubernatorial election.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-09-21, inclusive. Included only sources with explicitly verifiable publication dates on or before the cutoff; the latest included release is dated 2026-09-19. Excluded later reporting, undated live candidate pages, prediction-market and betting material, and a TSE calendar article whose displayed update date was after the cutoff; used the dated TRE-SC calendar article instead. Publication dates and factual passages were verified through web_search indexed source text. Direct web_fetch failed because multiple providers were registered, and the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned a rate-limit error, so full-page retrieval was unavailable. English excerpts are factual translations or condensations of the indexed Portuguese source text; Portuguese excerpts preserve source wording with minor punctuation normalization. No election outcome or post-cutoff development is included.
